deepdive.sec: Consumer Durables / Small Electrical Appliances & Induction Cooking

bull_bear.body: Debt repayment prioritized; Shift to Franchise-Owned/Franchise-Operated (FOFO) and Company-Owned/Franchise-Operated (COFO) models to reduce capital intensity of retail expansion; Inventory stocking (45-60 days) for raw materials to hedge against metal price inflation.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Forex volatility (significant loss in Q4); Raw material price inflation (Aluminum, Steel, Glass); Supply chain dependency on Chinese components (crystalline glass, magnets); Competition in e-commerce channel; Execution risk on rapid retail franchise rollout.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and aggressive on volume growth (>15% guidance); Pragmatic on margins (protecting 11% EBITDA while absorbing forex hits); Transparent on accounting distortions (lease liability, supplier credit); Focused on market share leadership in induction.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Retail store average sales increased from INR 3.8L to INR 4.7L, with breakeven at INR 2.5L, making new stores immediately accretive; Right-of-Use assets dropped from INR 160 Cr to INR 62 Cr due to accounting change (useful life reduced from 9 to 3 years), artificially depressing assets/liabilities; 97.7% volume growth in small appliances vs 12.7% value growth indicates a strategic mix shift to high-volume, lower-ASP entry-level products to capture market share.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Debt has been taken close to zero: current borrowings fell to ₹0.8 Cr at 31-Mar-26 from ₹179.5 Cr at 31-Mar-25 (₹140.9 Cr / ₹118.8 Cr in the two prior years), with non-current borrowings at ₹1.6 Cr.
- Funded by a step-change in operating cash: net cash from operating activities of ₹256.5 Cr in Mar-26 versus ₹129.9 Cr (Mar-25), ₹112.6 Cr (Mar-24) and ₹76.3 Cr (Mar-23), driven by a ₹119.2 Cr release from changes in working capital.
- Cash deployed to deleverage rather than distribute: financing cash outflow of ₹129.2 Cr in Mar-26 (vs ₹54.8 Cr in Mar-25), cash and cash equivalents up to ₹22.0 Cr from ₹2.8 Cr; the deck mentions no dividend or buyback.
- Lease liabilities were sharply reduced — non-current ₹35.3 Cr at 31-Mar-26 from ₹151.9 Cr, with right-to-use assets at ₹62.4 Cr from ₹159.7 Cr — consistent with the shift out of company-owned stores.
- Total equity of ₹504.2 Cr at 31-Mar-26 (share capital ₹33.1 Cr, other equity ₹471.1 Cr); RoCE of 12.0% (Mar-23), 12.3% (Mar-24), 12.3% (Mar-25) and 13.0% (Mar-26) — returns have been broadly flat despite the margin expansion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Induction Cooktops: 15.5% of revenue, +89.4% value growth, +67.3% volume growth; Small Appliances: 40.2% of revenue, +12.7% value growth, +97.7% volume growth (mix shift to lower ASP items); Cookware: Strong premiumization from aluminum to stainless steel; HoReCa: New 3,500W infrared launch.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Multi-brand approach to capture the entire value chain": Pigeon at the Value tier, described as a "20+ year old brand" and "one of the market leaders for certain products such as cookware" (sourced to an F&S Report), and Gilma at the Semi-Premium tier.
- Gilma is a distinct route to market, not just a label — "launched in 2016 and manufacturing commenced in 2019", it "offers a modular kitchen experience", "comprises chimneys, hobs and cooktops across price ranges and designs", and is "sold exclusively through Gilma branded outlets, which are owned and operated by franchisees", with a Gilma-specific mobile app for post-sales service requests.
- Brand-wise sales show the Pigeon-led concentration widening: the Pigeon series runs 226.8 → 235.4 → 270.1 → 403.4 (INR Cr, Q1 FY24 → Q1 FY27), OEM 38.8 → 58.3 → 65.7 → 73.3, and "Others*" shrinking 26.4 → 14.6 → 4.4 → 3.2.
- Gross-margin expansion is attributed to brand strength rather than price: margins expanded "despite ongoing supply chain challenges and elevated raw material costs, underscoring the company's healthy brand recall and operational excellence".
- Product breadth spans cookware (pressure cooker, wonder cast, non-stick, electric rice cookers, titanium hard anodized), cooktops and kitchen solutions (hobs, glass/stainless steel/induction cooktops, chimneys), small appliances (mixer grinders, blenders, kettles, toasters, air fryers, electric grills and more) and other products (emergency lamps, flasks, vacuum cleaners, BLDC fan, personal grooming), alongside LED bulbs, battens, downlights, kitchen sinks and water heaters.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [IKEA partnership] The milestones slide records the company having "entered into a strategic partnership with IKEA to develop cookware products" (the extract's year labels are unbound, so the date is not asserted here).
- [Demand shock] The induction upcycle is explicitly tied to an external event: "With the sudden dearth of LPG gas cylinders, the country saw a sudden spike in the purchase of induction cooktops", and the ICT commentary references "pre-war levels" — a demand driver outside management's control.
- [Working capital contradiction] The deck gives two different readings of the same 45-day figure: highlight 05 says "net working capital increased to 45 days from 23 days in Q4FY26, reflecting a strategic inventory build-up ahead of the festive season", while the working-capital note says "despite festive season inventory build-up, inventory days improved to 45 from 69 in Q1FY26". Separately the working-capital bar chart shows inventory days of 158, receivable days 28 and payable days 140 for Q1FY27 (FY25: 144/33/113; FY26: 133/26/136). Both readings are recorded as printed; no reconciliation is attempted.
- [Marketing scale] The "Ex Ko Karo Exchange" campaign reviving the Pigeon exchange offer reported 43.5 million reach, 6.3 million YouTube views, 1.27 million clicks and 30k+ high-intent leads, supported by national print ads, PR in national and vernacular publications, influencer/vox-pop content and point-of-sale branding.
- [Board addition] Mr. Chandru Kalro, former Managing Director of TTK Prestige Limited, sits on the board as Non-Executive Independent Director, bringing "over 35 years of leadership experience in the consumer durables industry" — a direct competitor pedigree on the board.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margin stable at 38.6% despite commodity inflation (Aluminum/Steel) due to 10% price hikes passed in Q4; EBITDA margin expanded 113 bps to 9.5%; Opex grew 41% YoY driven by sales commissions (franchise model), freight, and warranty provisions aligned with 32% sales growth.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: >15% for FY27 (confidence in 30% run-rate); Margin: Protect 11% EBITDA, target 42% Gross Margin in 2-3 years (+1% annually); Order Inflow: Induction demand > capacity; Capex: ~INR 40 Cr for FY27 (maintenance & minor lines), major cycle complete.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Demand for induction cooktops exceeds current 4-5 Mn unit annualized capacity; IKEA pipeline valued at INR 200-250 Cr at full capacity (3 lines phasing in through FY27); Export orders normalizing post-tariff reduction.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: IKEA global sourcing (INR 200-250 Cr potential); US export market reopening (tariff drop to 18%); Retail store network scaling to 500 by 2027 (currently 329); Capacity utilization upside beyond 5 Mn units.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Stove Kraft leveraged geopolitical tailwinds (Iran war, US tariff cuts) and backward integration to drive 32.4% Q4 revenue growth, with induction cooktops surging 89.4% YoY. The commencement of IKEA billing and a shift to franchise-led retail expansion position the company for sustained >15% CAGR, though near-term PAT is suppressed by forex volatility and accounting changes on lease liabilities.
